title: Slow Inventory Service
scenario: Storefront displays a product and asks Inventory whether it is in stock. Investigate what happens when Inventory responds very slowly.
learningObjectives: Connect response latency to a downstream dependency.
Validate a short timeout and graceful fallback.

instructions.title: Measure the normal system
instructions.body: Start normal traffic and capture a baseline. A baseline is the behavior you expect before a controlled failure.

instructions.title: State your hypothesis
instructions.body: Describe what you expect a 1500 ms Inventory delay to do, and why.

instructions.title: Inject latency
instructions.body: Make Inventory respond 1500 ms slower and measure the effect on Storefront.

instructions.title: Observe the impact
instructions.body: Compare response latency and success rate with your baseline, then record what changed.

instructions.title: Improve and validate
instructions.body: Apply a resilience option and repeat exactly the same latency experiment.

hints: A useful hypothesis mentions both a metric and the Inventory dependency.
A product page can remain useful even when stock information is temporarily unavailable.

resilienceOptions.label: Wait up to 10 seconds
resilienceOptions.description: The request remains coupled to a slow dependency.

resilienceOptions.label: Retry every request
resilienceOptions.description: Retries add load and do not make a slow dependency respond sooner.

resilienceOptions.label: Use a short timeout and graceful fallback
resilienceOptions.description: Return product details promptly and state that stock information is unavailable.

resilienceOptions.label: Ignore the slow dependency
resilienceOptions.description: Leave the current behavior unchanged and observe whether it improves.
